# op-hello

> A Python library and CLI for resolving 1Password `op://` references. It supports Windows Hello through the Windows desktop app from native Windows and WSL, and uses the native 1Password CLI on macOS and Linux.

The installable distribution is `op-hello`; Python applications import `op_hello`. The `op-hello` and `oph` commands are aliases to the same CLI. Use `oph version release patch` for Verkit-managed releases. Secret values are returned to the caller and are not written to diagnostic logs.

## Start here

- [Full agent guide](llms-full.txt): platform behavior, installation, API, CLI, configuration, caching, and security details.
- [README](README.md): installation and quick examples.

## API and implementation

- [Python API](src/op_hello/__init__.py): `read`, `resolve`, `is_available`, and `clear_cache`.
- [Python CLI entry point](src/op_hello/cli.py): platform dispatch and Verkit release commands for `op-hello` and `oph`.
- [Shell helper](bin/op-hello): CLI protocol, native Unix CLI, and WSL-to-Windows routing.
- [Windows reader](windows/op-read.ps1): `op.exe`, Windows Hello integration, DPAPI cache, and optional AutoHotkey pause.
- [Package metadata](pyproject.toml): dependencies, supported Python version, entry point, and packaged helpers.

- [Agent implementation guide](AGENTS.md): architecture, security, and release practices.
